clue.text: Small piece of mushroom without top of stalk

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the mushroom goes round the other letter

parts.note: a morel is an edible mushroom with a honeycombed cap

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of stalk

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of mushroom, with the stalk's tip trimmed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as minus, but here it means outside: S (top of stalk) is put inside MOREL.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small mouthful or bit of food, so it fits a small piece.

clue.text: Dance, though Rachel and son not dancing

indicators.note: letters that are dancing are moving about, so this signals a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A dance performed although neither Rachel nor her son is dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' is the anagram signal for RACHEL, S and NOT together.
explanation.definitionFit: The Charleston is a lively 1920s dance named after the city in South Carolina.

clue.text: Aggressor's press release to editor returning duty list

parts.note: PR is short for public relations, the source of press releases

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so this list is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a list setting out who is on duty when

explanation.surface: An aggressive party's press release passes to the editor, who sends back the duty list.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator preys on others, so it is an attacker or aggressor.

clue.text: Tamper with retro piece of religious iconography outside court

indicators.note: the reversed word sits outside the court abbreviation, holding it
retro means backward-looking, so the word for the iconography is turned round

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen

explanation.surface: Someone interfering with an old-fashioned religious image displayed outside a law court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retro' turns the cross into DOOR, which sits 'outside' the court; a rood is the large crucifix in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to falsify or interfere with it, the same as tampering.

clue.text: Return said sources of 3, 7, 15 and 9 for all those who have left their homeland

definitions.text: all those who have left their homeland

indicators.note: to return something is to send it back, so the word said is read in reverse
the source of a word is where it starts, so the opening letter of each named answer is taken

parts.note: the answer to 3 down
the answer to 7 down
the answer to 15 across
the answer to 9 across

explanation.surface: Instructions to go back over certain answers, presented as a puzzle about emigrants.
explanation.walkthrough: The bare numbers stand for the answers to those clues, and 'Return' reverses 'said' to give DIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is a people scattered away from their ancestral land, taken collectively.

clue.text: Drama changed into half comedy for produce some spice

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the other piece, which surrounds them
half of a six-letter word is its first three letters
changed signals that these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A drama turned half into comedy, as if to put on a little spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns DRAMA into ARDAM, which goes 'into' COM, the first half of comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic seed pod used as a spice in Indian and Scandinavian cooking.

clue.text: Plant found by fish next to part of canal network

parts.note: the char is a trout-like freshwater fish
a lock is the gated section that raises or lowers boats on a canal

explanation.surface: A plant spotted growing near a fish beside a canal lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlock is wild mustard, a yellow-flowered weed of fields.

clue.text: Old writer in annual golf event

parts.note: a pen is something that writes

explanation.surface: An elderly author takes part in the yearly golf tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Open is golf's oldest major championship, held every year.

clue.text: Bird originally kept in tiny enclosure

indicators.note: what something is originally is how it starts, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A bird first kept in a small cage.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a bird of prey with a forked tail, such as the red kite.

clue.text: Medical emergency caused by a speaker's inactivity

indicators.note: what a speaker produces is heard, not read, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a rest is a period of inactivity

explanation.surface: A medical crisis brought on by a lecturer sitting idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a rest' said out loud matches the answer; 'speaker's' looks like a person's but signals the sound, and the extra R is only in the spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac arrest, the heart stopping, is the medical emergency meant.

clue.text: Slope in garden altered to accommodate one plant finally

indicators.note: the rearranged letters make room for the numeral, holding it inside
altered means changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A sloping garden reshaped to make room for one more plant at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' turns GARDEN into GRADEN, which 'to accommodate' holds I; T comes from 'plant finally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the steepness of a slope, and also the slope itself.

clue.text: Fruit with extremely likeable fragrance has a fine lustre

definitions.note: a verb phrase defining an adjective: pearlescent describes something that has such a lustre

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: a scent is a fragrance

explanation.surface: A fruit with a pleasant smell and a glossy sheen.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the definition is a verb phrase for an adjective; read it as 'that has a fine lustre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearlescent means having the soft iridescent sheen of a pearl.

clue.text: Dish of beef roast, carved up with good source of nutrients, is no longer on the menu

indicators.note: meat carved up is cut into new pieces, so these letters are rearranged
the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

parts.note: a dish no longer available in a restaurant is off

explanation.surface: A beef dish whose roast has been carved and served with goodness is now off the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved up' rearranges ROAST and G into STROGA; N is the 'source of nutrients'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef stroganoff is strips of beef cooked in a sour cream sauce, a classic Russian dish.

clue.text: Creative type's gender is fluid

indicators.note: something fluid has no fixed shape, so these letters are poured into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A creative person who identifies as gender-fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluid' looks like part of a description of identity but is the anagram signal for GENDER IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer is someone whose work is creating the look of clothes, products or spaces.

clue.text: Flag flown by ship crossing river

indicators.note: the ship crosses the river by holding it in its middle

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship

explanation.surface: A flag flying from a ship as it crosses a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant flown from a mast.

clue.text: College head leaves part-time judge to request another delivery

indicators.note: the letter leaves, taken out of the word for the judge

parts.note: in England a recorder is a barrister who sits as a part-time judge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of a college walks out on a part-time judge to order something again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'College head' gives C, which 'leaves' RECORDER. In England a recorder is a part-time judge of the Crown Court.
explanation.definitionFit: To reorder is to order the same goods again, asking for a further supply.

clue.text: Two notes put away following Norway leader's command

indicators.note: following places the eating piece after the Norway letter

parts.note: do and mi are two notes of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to put away food is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: An order from the head of Norway, after two notes were filed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts ATE after N, the first letter of Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: To command something is to have control over it, to dominate it.

clue.text: Huge flow of gold found in British river

indicators.note: the gold is found inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A great flood of gold discovered in a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a fast, violent rush of water or anything else.

clue.text: Wise men given no time to join those waiting to see old French fortifications

parts.note: the Magi are the wise men of the Nativity
people waiting in turn form a line, a queue

explanation.surface: The wise men, short of time, join a queue to visit old French forts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maginot Line was France's chain of defences along the German border before the Second World War.

clue.text: Very sad soldier in vehicle going back uphill

indicators.note: the soldier sits inside the reversed vehicle
in a down entry, going uphill means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in a cart rolling back up a hill: a sad sight.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'going back uphill' reads bottom to top, making TRAC, and 'in' puts the soldier inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something causing great sorrow, deeply sad.

clue.text: Covers over notice

indicators.note: turned over, this down entry reads in reverse

parts.note: tops are lids or covers

explanation.surface: Lids placed over a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Detective in touch with politician's solicitor

parts.note: PI stands for private investigator, a detective
MP, a Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A detective contacts a politician's lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but means one who solicits on behalf of sex workers.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimp touts for clients for prostitutes, so solicits trade.

clue.text: Sharp fielder catching good new Australian

indicators.note: the fielder catches the letters, holding them inside

parts.note: point is a fielding position on the off side in cricket

explanation.surface: An alert fielder catches a promising new Australian batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: POINT is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant can mean keenly felt or piercing, as in sharp pain or sharp regret.

clue.text: Relative trapping animal in bottle

indicators.note: the relative traps the animal by holding it inside

parts.note: mam is a dialect word for mother
the gnu is an African antelope, the wildebeest

explanation.surface: A relative traps a creature in a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a wine bottle holding twice the standard amount.

clue.text: Court official with gratuities for office workers

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity; the plural here strictly gives a spare S
the staff are the workers of an office

explanation.surface: A court official given tips for the office team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gratuities' should give TIPS, leaving an extra S; read it as TIP to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer who enforces orders, named after the metal-tipped staff once carried.

clue.text: Reflect, as young person runs for navy

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a minor is someone under the age of adulthood
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, so two runs give two Rs

explanation.surface: A young person thinks back on running away to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the N (navy) in MINOR for RR: runs, plural, means two Rs, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: To mirror something is to reflect it back as a looking-glass does.
